key_insight: A DFT-trained high-dimensional neural network potential can reproduce subtle martensitic energetics and finite-temperature structural behavior in NiTi with atomistic fidelity.
engineering_relevance: This enables large-scale, nanosecond molecular dynamics of NiTi shape-memory alloys to study phase stability, twinning, and deformation mechanisms beyond the reach of direct DFT.
method: Trained an HDNNP on DFT reference data for martensitic NiTi.
Validated against equilibrium structures, elastic constants, stacking-fault energies, and vibrational spectra.
Used finite-temperature molecular dynamics to probe unconstrained structural evolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate reproduction of B19′ vs B33 stability and meV/atom-level energy differences, along with strong agreement for elastic and vibrational properties.
watch_item: Transferability may still be limited outside the DFT training domain, especially for defects, compositions, or temperatures not represented in the dataset.
paper_title: A high-dimensional neural network potential for finite-temperature phenomena in NiTi martensite
